children: Micron Technology (MU, Financials), is getting another boost from the AI-driven memory boom as stronger-than-expected DRAM pricing prompted Citi to raise its earnings estimates and price target.

Citi analyst Atif Malik now expects Micron to generate $51 billion in fiscal fourth-quarter sales and $31.45 in EPS, slightly above consensus. For fiscal first-quarter 2027, he sees sales reaching $57 billion and EPS of $35.25.

The revisions come as memory pricing continues to run hotter than expected. Citi raised its assumptions for both DRAM and NAND, forecasting blended DRAM average selling prices to rise 20% sequentially in fiscal fourth quarter and another 13% in the following quarter.

AI demand is keeping the memory market tight. Malik expects both DRAM and NAND to remain undersupplied for the foreseeable future, although he expects pricing growth to slow over the next four quarters and peak around the second quarter of 2027.
Citi also expects Micron to spend about $50 billion on capital expenditures in fiscal 2027, including more than $20 billion on equipment.
Malik reiterated a Buy rating and raised his price target to $1,300 from $1,150.
Micron shares were down about 0.8% in premarket trading Wednesday, following a huge run that has pushed the company's market value above $1 trillion.
The next catalyst is Micron's upcoming earnings report, which should show whether pricing strength is translating into the revenue and profit growth Citi expects.

title: Micron's Memory Boom Is Showing Up in Prices
